title: October 21: barriers, gates and measured closure
summary: BrainBox drift repair and a retention/replacement tradeoff lead to finite winding cells and selectively writable arrays. Both Alexander repositories now have working engineered memory components, while ordinary three-well controls remove topology necessity and a discrete address latch removes the demonstrated need for analog address state. Sol first single-query gate stays failed; its separately locked five-query array passes. Claude heat-gating succeeds after a drive-geometry correction, using endpoint oracle checks. Noise Sea behavior reverses between ordered domains and melted sea; it is not physical mass or time dilation. Closure concerns these bounded tests, not near-optimality or a new AI paradigm. The missing traffic-driven choice of where and what to retain needs an external task and conventional benchmark before further claims. Receipts inspected; upstream simulations were not rerun for this atlas pass.

nodes.claim: Finite 2-D noisy complex-field loops test phase diffusion, winding barriers, weak-link lifetime and global-value/local-material-or-heat gated writing.
nodes.survived: Phase diffusion is quantitatively connected to temperature and field amplitude. Small winding integers survive weak local reads. A finite clasp holds n=1 across about 1.5 coherence lengths in the tested geometry. Four-ring arrays with per-hole flux give 120/120 material-gated target requests and 117/120 heat-gated requests, with 0/360 endpoint crosstalk each.
nodes.killed: A phase alone has no barrier; large winding alphabets and a reliable single local read fail. Whole-box rotation causes crosstalk. The winding arrays use full-field oracle reads, supplied addresses and values; requests include no-ops (79/79 and 70/73 actual changes). Ordinary three-well success in Sol removes topology necessity. Infinite horned-sphere claims and physical/AI superiority are not established.
nodes.era: October 21: a finite barrier and a local write gate

nodes.claim: A 64-site winding cell and then a three-cell array test deliberate replacement, local read cost and selective access against discrete-address and ordinary three-well controls.
nodes.survived: First gate: 240/240 replacements and 240/240 closed retentions, with no monitored damage across 100 reads per history. The independently locked array: 120/120 writes, 240/240 protected bystander exposures, 120/120 correct whole-array endpoints and 357/360 five-query votes per trace/snap/oracle arm. Exact-source full replay compares 588,917 floats with zero difference.
nodes.killed: First single-query gate fails at 92.72%; later five-query criteria do not rescue it. Ordinary wells match or exceed both winding tests. Analog address benefit fails with zero gain over a discrete latch. Cue ports, reset/trigger markers and command values are supplied; diagnostic arrays preclude a physical two-bit implementation claim. No topology necessity, learned routing, energy advantage or scalable associative recall is demonstrated.
nodes.era: October 21: addressed memory works; richer state earns no benefit

edges.why: AlexandersBrain explicitly starts from VMNClaude phase drift and read disturbance, then tests winding barriers rather than claiming code inheritance.
AlexandersBrain names BrainBoxClaude as motivation; local heat later supplies an engineered access gate. The traffic-driven learning loop remains unbuilt.
The design explicitly responds to BrainBoxSol local slowness retaining old traces while resisting replacement; a temporary access gate addresses the component question.
Claude Part 2 explicitly takes Sol gated writing into 2-D and an array. This is conceptual/mechanistic convergence, not a code fork or matched performance comparison.
The addressed follow-up reads Claude finite-gap and memory comparison, corrects gate-only erasure, and tests repeated selective updates with a conventional control.

motifs.title: A barrier holds; a global value and local gate replace
motifs.description: Small winding and ordinary multi-well memories can perform write/hold/read/replace. Engineered access succeeds without establishing topology necessity, learned allocation or a product advantage.

motifs.title: Let an ordinary control remove the stronger claim
motifs.description: Noise-aware writing fails; retention can resist replacement; ordinary wells match winding cells and an address symbol matches an analog trace. Record useful mechanisms separately from unsupported necessity and efficiency claims.

motifs.title: Noise changes order; slowing depends on the phase and observable
motifs.description: PhiWorld effective mode frequency and prescribed propagation coefficient respond differently inside a domain and in the melted sea. A slow mode near melting is a model diagnostic, not physical mass creation or relativistic time dilation.
